title: Homeschooling Hits Record Numbers
titleZh: 信任崩塌：美国家长正在集体抛弃公立学校
summary:
无论被称为在家上学还是家庭自主教育，这种由家庭主导的学习方式在美国已经流行多年，背后反映的是人们对传统公立学校的失望，包括僵化的体系、日益政治化的倾向，以及实打实的教学效果不佳。新冠疫情期间，这一趋势更是被显著推动：长时间的停课和混乱的远程教学，促使许多家庭开始尝试亲自教育孩子。但当时的关键问题在于，随着公共卫生管控措施的解除，人们对在家教育的兴趣是否也会随之减弱？如今答案已经明朗，这种情况并未发生。美国人对家庭自主教育的兴趣仍在持续上升。

来源：Reason；作者：J.D. Tuccille；原文发布时间：2025-11-26 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Whether called homeschooling or DIY education, family-directed learning has been growing in popularity for years in the U.S. alongside disappointment in the rigidity, politicization, and flat-out poor results of traditional public schools. That growth was supercharged during the COVID-19 pandemic when extended closures and bumbled remote learning drove many families to experiment with teaching their own kids. The big question was whether the end of public health controls would also curtail interest in homeschooling. We know now that it didn't. Americans' taste for DIY education is on the rise.
paragraphs.contentZh: 无论被称为在家上学还是家庭自主教育，这种由家庭主导的学习方式在美国已经流行多年，背后反映的是人们对传统公立学校的失望，包括僵化的体系、日益政治化的倾向，以及实打实的教学效果不佳。新冠疫情期间，这一趋势更是被显著推动：长时间的停课和混乱的远程教学，促使许多家庭开始尝试亲自教育孩子。但当时的关键问题在于，随着公共卫生管控措施的解除，人们对在家教育的兴趣是否也会随之减弱？如今答案已经明朗，这种情况并未发生。美国人对家庭自主教育的兴趣仍在持续上升。

paragraphs.contentEn: "In the 2024-2025 school year, homeschooling continued to grow across the United States, increasing at an average rate of 5.4%," Angela Watson of the Johns Hopkins University School of Education's Homeschool Hub wrote earlier this month. "This is nearly three times the pre-pandemic homeschooling growth rate of around 2%." She added that more than a third of the states from which data is available report their highest homeschooling numbers ever, even exceeding the peaks reached when many public and private schools were closed during the pandemic.
paragraphs.contentZh: 约翰斯·霍普金斯大学教育学院“在家教育中心”的安吉拉·沃森在本月早些时候撰文指出：“2024—2025学年，全美在家教育人数继续增长，平均增幅达到5.4%，几乎是疫情前约2%增长率的三倍。”她补充说，在已有数据的州中，超过三分之一报告的在家教育人数创下历史新高，甚至超过疫情期间公立和私立学校大面积停课时的峰值。

paragraphs.contentEn: After COVID-19 public health measures were suspended, there was a brief drop in homeschooling as parents and families returned to old habits. That didn't last long. Homeschooling began surging again in the 2023-2024 school year, with that growth continuing last year. Based on numbers from 22 states (not all states have released data, and many don't track homeschoolers), four report declines in the ranks of homeschooled children—Delaware, the District of Columbia, Hawaii, and Tennessee—while the others report growth from around 1 percent (Florida and Louisiana) to as high as 21.5 percent (South Carolina).
paragraphs.contentZh: 在新冠疫情相关的公共卫生措施解除后，随着许多家庭逐渐恢复原有生活节奏，在家教育的热度曾出现短暂回落。但这一趋势并未持续太久。到2023—2024学年，在家教育再次出现强劲增长，并在去年继续保持上升势头。根据22个州的统计数据来看（并不是所有州都会发布相关数据，且许多州并不统计在家受教育人数），仅特拉华州、哥伦比亚特区、夏威夷州和田纳西州四个地区报告了在家教育人数的下降；其余各州均呈现增长态势，增幅从约1%（如佛罗里达和路易斯安那）到最高的21.5%（南卡罗来纳）。

paragraphs.contentEn: The latest figures likely underestimate growth in homeschooling since not all DIY families abide by registration requirements where they exist, and because families who use the portable funding available through increasingly popular Education Savings Accounts to pay for homeschooling costs are not counted as homeschoolers in several states, Florida included. As a result, adds Watson, "we consider these counts as the minimum number of homeschooled students in each state."
paragraphs.contentZh: 最新的统计数据很可能低估了在家教育的实际增长，一方面，并不是所有选择自主教育的家庭都会遵守各地现有的登记要求；另一方面，随着教育储蓄账户的普及，越来越多的家庭使用这类可支配资金来支付在家教育的相关费用，但在包括佛罗里达在内的多个州，这类家庭并不会在统计中被算作在家受教育群体。因此，沃森补充说，“我们只将这些数字视为各州在家教育学生人数的最低估计。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Recent estimates put the total homeschooling population at about 6 percent of students across the United States, compared to about 3 percent pre-pandemic. Continued growth necessarily means the share of DIY-educated students is increasing. That's quite a change for an education approach that was decidedly not mainstream just a generation ago. "This isn't a pandemic hangover; it's a fundamental shift in how American families are thinking about education," comments Watson.
paragraphs.contentZh: 最新估算显示，目前全美约有6%的学生在家接受教育，而疫情前这一比例大约为3%。持续的增长意味着接受家庭自主教育的学生占比正在不断上升。对于一种在上一代人眼中还远非主流的教育方式而言，这已是相当显著的变化。沃森评论道：“这不是疫情留下的短期效应；这是美国家庭教育观念发生的根本性转变。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Homeschooling is a major beneficiary of changing education preferences among American families, but it's not the only one. "Five years after the pandemic's onset, there has been a substantial shift away from public schools and toward non-public options," Boston University's Joshua Goodman and Abigail Francis wrote last summer for Education Next. Looking at Massachusetts—not the friendliest regulatory environment for alternatives to traditional public schooling—they found that as the state's school-age population shrank by 2.6 percent since 2019, there has been a 4.2 percent decline in local public-school enrollment, a 0.7 decline in private-school enrollment, and a 56 percent increase in homeschooling. "Charter school enrollment is flat, due in part to regulatory limitations in Massachusetts," they added.
paragraphs.contentZh: 美国家庭教育风向的转变，让在家教育成为主要的赢家，但并非唯一。波士顿大学的约书亚·古德曼和阿比盖尔·弗朗西斯去年夏天在《Education Next》上撰文指出：“疫情爆发五年后，学生从公立学校向非公立教育体系的转移已十分明显。”以马萨诸塞州为例（该州对传统公立学校以外的教育选择监管较为严格），他们发现，自2019年以来，该州学龄人口下降了2.6%，但当地公立学校的入学人数却减少了4.2%，私立学校入学人数下降0.7%，而在家教育人数则增长了56%。他们补充说：“至于特许学校，受马萨诸塞州监管限制的影响，其入学人数基本保持稳定。”

paragraphs.contentEn: In research published in August, Dylan Council, Sofoklis Goulas, and Faidra Monachou of the Brookings Institution found similar results at the national level. "The COVID-19 pandemic forced millions of families to rethink where and how their children learn, and the effects continue to reshape American K-12 education," they observed. If "parents keep choosing alternatives at the pace observed since 2020, traditional public schools could lose as many as 8.5 million students, shrinking from 43.06 million in 2023-24 to as few as 34.57 million by mid-century." It's not difficult to figure out what pushes parents to seek out alternatives and to flock to the various forms of DIY education grouped under the homeschooling heading.
paragraphs.contentZh: 布鲁金斯学会的迪伦·康塞尔、索福克利斯·古拉斯和法德拉·莫纳丘在今年8月发布的研究中，也在全美范围得出了类似结论。他们指出：“新冠疫情迫使数百万家庭重新思考孩子在哪里、以及以何种方式接受教育，这一影响至今仍在重塑美国的K-12教育体系。”研究进一步预测，如果“家长继续以自2020年以来的节奏选择替代性教育路径，那么传统公立学校可能会流失多达850万名学生，在本世纪中叶，学生规模或将从2023—2024学年的4306万减少到仅3457万。”至于是什么推动家长不断寻求各类替代方案，并转向被统称为“在家教育”的多种家庭自主教育模式，原因其实并不难理解。

paragraphs.contentEn: "The fraction of parents saying K-12 education is heading in the wrong direction was fairly stable from 2019 to 2022 but rose in 2023 and then again in 2024 to its highest level in a decade, suggesting continuing or even growing frustration with schools," commented Goodman and Francis. Specifically, EdChoice's Schooling in America survey puts the percentage of school parents saying that K-12 education is headed in the right direction at 41 percent—down from 48 percent in 2022 (the highest score recorded). Fifty-nine percent say K-12 education is on the wrong track—up from 52 percent in 2021 (the lowest score recorded).
paragraphs.contentZh: 古德曼和弗朗西斯指出：“从2019年至2022年，认为K-12教育方向有问题的家长比例总体保持稳定，但这一比例在2023年出现上升，并在2024年再次攀升至十年来的最高水平，这表明家长对学校的失望情绪仍在持续，甚至可能进一步加剧。”具体而言，EdChoice 发布的“美国学校教育”调查显示，认为K-12教育方向正确的在校生家长占比为41%——低于2022年的48%（该调查记录的最高值）；而认为教育方向错误的家长比例为59%，高于2021年的52%（该调查记录的最低值）。

paragraphs.contentEn: When asked if they are satisfied with their children's education, public school parents consistently rank last after parents who choose private schools, homeschooling, and charter schools. Importantly, among all parents of school-age children, homeschooling enjoys a 70 percent favorability rating. The reasons for the move away from public schools certainly vary from family to family, but there have been notable developments in recent years. During the pandemic, many parents discovered that their preferences regarding school closures and health policies were anything but a priority for educators.
paragraphs.contentZh: 在被问及是否对孩子所受教育感到满意时，公立学校家长的满意度始终低于选择私立学校、在家教育和特许学校的家长。值得注意的是，在所有学龄儿童家长中，有70%对在家教育持正面看法。当然，每个家庭选择离开公立学校的原因各不相同，但近年来一些显著的变化值得关注。疫情期间，许多家长意识到，在停课安排和健康政策等关键决策上，他们的意愿并未被优先考虑。

paragraphs.contentEn: Closures also gave parents a chance to experience public schools' competence with remote learning, and many were unimpressed. They have also been unhappy with the poor quality and often politicized lessons taught to their children that infuriatingly blend declining learning outcomes with indoctrination. That doesn't mean parents all want the same things, but the one-size-fits-some nature of public schooling make curriculum battles inevitable—and push many towards the exits in favor of alternatives including, especially, homeschooling. The shift appears to be here to stay.
paragraphs.contentZh: 学校的停课也让家长得以亲身领教公立学校的远程教学能力，而许多人对实际效果并不满意。与此同时，课程质量的下降以及日益政治化的教学内容也让家长感到不满，且这种一方面导致学生成绩持续走低、另一方面进行意识形态灌输的教育方式，更令他们难以接受。当然，这并不意味着所有家长的诉求完全一致，但公立教育那种“只适合一部分人”的单一模式，使课程之争难以避免——最终将促使许多家庭转向其他教育选择，特别是在家教育。种种迹象表明，这一转变显然将长期持续。

paragraphs.contentEn: "What's particularly striking is the resilience of this trend," concludes Watson of Johns Hopkins University's Homeschool Hub. "States that saw declines have bounced back with double-digit growth, and we're seeing record enrollment numbers across the country." Once an alternative way to educate children, homeschooling is now an increasingly popular and mainstream option.
paragraphs.contentZh: 约翰斯·霍普金斯大学“在家教育中心”的沃森总结说：“这一趋势最引人注目的地方，在于它的持续增长力。那些此前出现数据下滑的州，如今都以两位数的增幅明显反弹；放眼全国，我们正在看到创纪录的在家教育人数。”曾经被视为传统教育的替代路径，在家教育如今正迅速走向普及、甚至日益成为主流选择。
